page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v7 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine within the Dadsv7 family, powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core running 2 threads per core, with CPU speeds reaching up to 4.5 GHz. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and machine learning instruction support via AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration with AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The host provides 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 118 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial disparity between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core processing ranks in the top tier across several workloads, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2775.0 and top-tier throughput in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests. In contrast, parallel performance is constrained by the two-thread limit. Multi-core Geekbench, PassMark CPU scores, and software compilation benchmarks register in the lower quartile of cloud systems. Large block uncached memory bandwidth sustains balanced middle-tier rates of 45.49 GB/sec read and 34.03 GB/sec write. Network and socket handling capabilities, such as Redis SET operations and static web serving, similarly reflect the boundaries of the 2-vCPU sizing.

Resource allocation on the D2ads_v7 emphasizes qualitative cost efficiency for compute profiles dependent on high frequency rather than wide parallel scaling. The integrated 118 GB NVMe local disk delivers fast scratch storage without requiring additional attached premium disks for temporary caching. The instance architecture aligns with low-concurrency web hosting, lightweight microservices, continuous integration build agents with single-thread bottlenecks, and entry-level background processing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core with two execution threads, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. It features modern instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves top-tier single-core compute performance, as reflected in high Geekbench and single-threaded compression scores. However, aggregate multi-core throughput remains restricted by the two-vCPU footprint, placing overall multi-threaded metrics in lower performance quartiles. The 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio provides efficient resource balance for entry-tier enterprise deployments. Microsoft Azure D2ads_v7 is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, development environments, lightweight web hosting, microservices, and modest data processing pipelines requiring high clock frequency and low-latency local scratch disk.
